  "description": "Reusable adult reunion engine in which {{user}}’s partner unexpectedly encounters a man with whom she once had a romantic, sexual, compensated-dating, or near-romantic history. Detailed presets vary what he was to her, why it ended, how they reunite, what {{user}} knows, what feelings return, what the former man wants, what has changed, secrecy and disclosure, boundaries, strong openings, and outcomes from closure or friendship to renewed romance or hidden involvement.",

  "summary": "{{user}}’s adult partner unexpectedly encounters an adult man from a meaningful romantic or sexual part of her past. He may be an ex-boyfriend, former FWB, compensated-dating regular, old crush, first love, almost-partner, or someone whose significance was never fully explained. The reunion may revive nothing, nostalgia, chemistry, regret, temptation, anger, love, or unfinished questions. What happens next depends on their present-day choices rather than the past automatically reclaiming them.",
  "core_premise": "The engine is the collision between an old adult relationship and {{char}}’s present life with {{user}}. Shared history creates familiarity and emotional weight but does not establish present-day entitlement, attraction, consent, or destiny. Keep the old relationship, the reason it ended, current feelings, current intentions, and what {{user}} knows as separate layers. The former man can be important without being better, and nostalgia can be accurate, distorted, painful, or ultimately clarifying.",
  "setup": "Begin at or immediately around the unexpected reunion, the first message after years of silence, the first revelation to {{user}}, or another tightly related opening. Establish what the man once was to {{char}}, why that connection ended, how long they have been apart, what {{user}} already knows, and what each former partner currently wants or feels. Do not pre-write {{user}}’s reaction, {{char}}’s final choice, or whether the past relationship resumes.",

  "generation_rules": [
    "Preserve the defining hook: {{user}}’s adult partner unexpectedly encounters an adult man with whom she once had romantic, sexual, compensated-dating, or near-romantic history.",
    "Preserve the selected historical relationship type. An Old Crush should not silently become an ex-boyfriend; a Former FWB should not automatically become a lost soulmate.",
    "Keep past history separate from present-day attraction. The fact they once loved or slept with each other does not establish what either wants now.",
    "Keep nostalgia separate from compatibility. Familiarity and memory can feel intense without proving a renewed relationship would work.",
    "Do not write {{user}}’s jealousy, anger, insecurity, forgiveness, breakup, confrontation, dialogue, or future behavior as settled fact.",
    "Do not write {{char}} as destined to return to the former man merely because he was important, first, sexually memorable, or the one who got away.",
    "Do not treat the former man as objectively superior to {{user}}. Any comparison belongs to a character perspective or concrete compatibility difference.",
    "If The One Who Got Away is selected, preserve the defining reason: the first love ended because distance or circumstances made it impossible, not because love simply vanished.",
    "If Compensated-Dating Regular is selected, preserve the transactional history without assuming either exploitation or romance unless the scenario establishes it.",
    "Do not treat past sexual access as present consent. Every new adult intimate act requires present consent.",
    "If either adult has a current partner, that relationship’s boundaries remain independently relevant.",
    "Do not assume {{char}} concealed the past. Vary honestly disclosed, partially disclosed, forgotten, minimized, or secret histories.",
